title: Introduce failure steward and compact snapshot exporter for prompt-set incidents
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Long-running prompt-set regressions and incident postmortems often require compact, reproducible artifacts that capture the minimal failing context. Existing snapshot exports are verbose and expensive to store when run across thousands of prompt variants. This PR introduces a lightweight 'failure steward' process that identifies stable failing exemplars and a compact snapshot exporter that emits an epsilon-sized archive suitable for rapid rollback evaluation and incident sharing. What this PR does: 1) Adds eval_harness/steward.py: a small stateful service that tracks per-prompt failure windows, coalesces redundant failures using token-level similarity heuristics, and selects up to N exemplar traces per regression event. 2) Adds eval_harness/snapshotter_compact.py: exporter that serializes exemplars, minimal model metadata (model hash, quantization flags), token-level diffs, and a provenance header to a compressed .tgz with a deterministic filename. 3) Integrates a new CI smoke integration (ci/integration/snapshot-compat.yaml) which verifies that compact snapshots can be round-tripped through the replay harness and that exported provenance matches recorded evaluation metadata. 4) Adds unit and integration tests (tests/test_steward.py, tests/test_snapshot_roundtrip.py) and example consumer tooling (examples/compact-replay/README.md) showing how to load and replay a compact snapshot locally. 5) Adds docs (docs/ops/compact-snapshots.md) describing the file format, retention recommendations, and suggested alert workflow. Compatibility and safety: the steward runs in read-only mode against eval outputs by default and requires explicit opt-in flags to persist artifacts. Compact exporter intentionally omits raw user data fields; we added a redact layer that strips PII-like tokens if the team enables the redact flag in the steward config. Testing and performance: a synthetic smoke harness was added to validate export size; typical exports for 1k failing prompts are ~25MB compressed (vs ~320MB for the full export path). We include benchmarks in the smoke CI job so future changes cannot regress export size by more than 2x without a human review. Rollout: feature is off by default. Ops can enable steward with ENV flags and a retention policy. Follow-ups: hook the steward to the alert router to auto-open incident tickets when exemplar counts exceed thresholds (ENG-5790), and add an upload adapter for S3/GS with server-side encryption (ENG-5791).

review_conversation: Omar: Overall this looks promising. Two questions: can you explain the token-similarity heuristic and whether it is deterministic across tokenizers? Maya: The heuristic uses a normalized byte-level subsequence similarity on token ids exported by the harness; we pin tokenizer versions in the provenance header to ensure determinism. Priya: Please add audit logs for when steward persists artifacts. Maya: Added audit events to the exporter and included a simple retention flag; pushed an update (see commit 3). Liam: Found a flaky test on CI referencing wall-clock timestamps in tests; suggest using a fake clock. Maya: Reworked the tests to use the test-clock fixture from tests/util/test_clock.py. After CI rerun the job passed and Omar approved. Priya approved with a docs suggestion which was applied. Merge method: squash and merge. Merge sha: a3c9f12
release_notes: Introduced a failure steward to coalesce failing prompt traces and a compact snapshot exporter for small reproducible incident artifacts. Opt-in; disabled by default. Adds CI smoke checks to prevent snapshot bloat.
notes_for_oncall: When enabling steward in production, set STEWARD_PERSIST=false and validate outputs in a staging bucket first. If replicas show >100 exemplars in a 1h window, silence auto-upload until investigation. The CI smoke job name is 'snapshot-compat-smoke' and will report export sizes under artifacts.
changelog_summary: feat(eval): compact snapshot exporter + failure steward for prompt-set incidents
